questions: What exactly does "count of integers" mean in each subarray - does it refer to the number of elements or the count of distinct integers?
Are the indices i and j inclusive or exclusive in defining the subarrays, and do they represent 0-based or 1-based indexing?
Can the subarrays contain zero elements, or must all three subarrays be non-empty as implied by the constraint 1 ≤ i < j ≤ N-1?
What is the exact format of the input - are the integers on the second line separated by spaces, tabs, or any whitespace?
What should be the output format - just the integer answer or should it include any additional formatting?
Are duplicate values in the sequence allowed, and if so, how do they affect the counting?
What is the expected behavior when N=3, the minimum possible value according to constraints?
Should the solution handle the case where all elements in a subarray are the same value, and how does that affect the count?

inline_prompts: This problem is a harder version of Problem C. Here, the sequence is split into three subarrays. You are given an integer sequence of length N: A = (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N). When splitting A at two positions into three non-empty subarrays, find the maximum possible sum of the counts in those subarrays. More formally, find the maximum sum of the following three values for a pair of integers (i,j) such that 1 \leq i < j \leq N-1: the count of integers in (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_i), the count of integers in (A_{i+1},A_{i+2},\ldots,A_j), and the count of integers in (A_{j+1},A_{j+2},\ldots,A_{N}). "Counts" refers to the number of distinct integers in each subarray. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N Output Print the answer. Constraints - 3 \leq N \leq 3 \times 10^5 - 1 \leq A_i \leq N (1 \leq i \leq N) - All input values are integers.
